en: Spin each wheel. Spot the trick and explain your choice.

Spin to unlock a discount coupon — up to 50% off!

This wheel is rigged: it is programmed to land on the 50% coupon every time. The other discounts are decoration, making a fixed offer look like a lucky win. You must then make a purchase to unlock the coupon and another to use it. The aim is to make you spend more.
The coupon gives me 50% off the purchase needed to unlock it.
It pushes me to buy once to unlock the coupon, then buy again to use it.
I can add the coupon to my account without buying anything.
Free spin! Try your luck for up to 10 game coins.

The offer is a chance to win up to 10 game coins, not a promise of 10 coins every time or money to withdraw. Smaller prizes and the visible no-prize slice fit that offer. This simulated wheel selects randomly; a few spins alone would not prove that a real wheel is fair.
It offers a chance at up to 10 game coins, so smaller prizes or no prize fit the offer.
Every free spin should give me the advertised 10 coins.
The coins I win can be withdrawn as real money.
Win a phone, a laptop or up to €100 — give it a spin!

This wheel forces “No prize”, then tempts you with another chance. The aim is to keep you spending time on the game. On a site with ads, that can mean more adverts seen. Another spin does not bring you closer to a win: in this simulated wheel, the prizes cannot be selected.
Seven prize slices guarantee I will win within eight spins.
Each loss makes the next spin more likely to win a big prize.
It keeps giving me nothing while using big prizes and “try again” to keep me playing.
Your free bonus spin: win up to 8 game points!

The offer is for game points, not cash or a shopping discount. Eight is the largest prize; smaller amounts and no prize are also shown on the wheel. This simulated draw is random. Winning or losing a few spins does not establish whether a real draw is fair.
These points give me a discount on my next purchase.
The offer is for game points, and the wheel openly includes a no-prize outcome.
“Up to 8 points” means I must receive at least 8 points.
